notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood. Ran 3-week Hosted API trial (Jan 4–Jan 25). Goal: replace multiple internal model endpoints with single unified inference layer; move to Dedicated for predictable unit economics and isolation. Primary features: in-app assistant for power users + help bot for support workflows + search reranking for logs.

Trial feedback (key picks):
- Integration: quick SDK integration, straightforward streaming. liked token-level cost breakdown in console.
- Latency: p95 ~180ms on hosted for our median prompts; peaks up to 420ms on longer sessions. p50 ~70ms.
- Stability: two days of elevated error rate during a 3rd-party region outage; auto-fallback to smaller model helped but we want Dedicated fallback policies.

Traffic & token mix observed during Hosted trial (production-like test traffic):
- Average sustained QPS during trial: 6 QPS (development traffic).
- Observed peak QPS during load tests: 92 QPS (30s burst tests).
- Typical concurrency observed: 4–10 concurrent sessions; peak concurrency in load tests: 28.
- Token mix (requests composition): 70% short interactions (<=64 tokens total), 25% mid-length (65–512 tokens), 5% long (>512 tokens) — long ones are analyst-style prompts with >1k tokens sometimes.
- Avg tokens per request (all): ~220 tokens (input+generated).

Production forecast (what they told us in sizing call):
- Month 1 (post-Dedicated): baseline 18 QPS sustained, avg concurrency 12, projected monthly tokens ~450M.
- Month 6 (scale expectation): baseline 45 QPS sustained, peak bursts ~380 QPS (marketing release windows), concurrency target for p95 latency target is 40.
- SLA target: p95 latency <250ms for chat flows; acceptable fallback latency <500ms.

Dedicated requirements they asked for in workshop:
- Initial Dedicated pool to support 50 QPS sustained, ability to burst to 400 QPS for up to 10 minutes (marketing spikes).
- Autoscaling window: scale up within 60–120s for predicted bursts (will use request-based routing + cache warming).
- KV/prefix caching expected for common prompts (20% hit rate) to reduce token compute.
- Model strategy: primary xl-compat model for quality; fall back to quantized medium for cost-sensitive bursts. Need guidance on quantization tradeoffs.

POC scope (requested):
- 2-week Dedicated staging POC: mirror production traffic (traffic replay), synthetic burst tests to 400 QPS, evaluate latency SLOs and unit token cost.
- Eval metrics: cost per 1M tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, prefix cache hit rate, autoscale reaction time.

Decision factors / buying signals:
- Need predictable billing for budget planning (finance wants committed reserved capacity number).
- Security: must pass SSO/SAML SSO + SOC2 check; data residency for EU customers.
- SE is running benchmarking scripts; asked for recommended GPU SKU and expected QPS per node for their primary model.

Direct quotes: "We want a clear mapping from our forecasted QPS/concurrency to committed GPUs and cost — finance will only sign if committed spend maps to predictable cost per MAU." — CTO (Anika R.)

Attachments / artifacts: trial logs uploaded to Drive (link above), Fireflies transcript 1/29 walkthrough, internal load test results (gated).
